posts.title: Your developer disappeared
posts.description: Someone built your software. They were good, or good enough. Then the replies got slower, then they stopped, and now there is an invoice arriving every month from an account nobody can log into and a website you are afraid to touch. This is the single most common reason people call me, and it is worth saying plainly: it is a recoverable situation almost every time. It does not feel that way from the inside, because the thing you have lost is not really the code. It is the ability to make a decision about your own business without asking someone who is not there.

posts.title: You inherited a codebase
posts.description: There are a few ways to end up here. You acquired a company and the software came with it. The founder who wrote it left. An agency built it, the contract ended, and the handover was a zip file. Or it has simply been running so long that everyone who understood it has moved on. However you got here, the position is the same: you own something that works, you cannot safely change it, and every estimate you get for touching it comes back either suspiciously cheap or unbelievably expensive.

posts.title: What a fractional CTO costs
posts.description: Fractional CTO pricing is all over the place, and most of what is published is written to sell you one. Here are the market ranges, what moves the number, and how I price my own work. The market, in real numbers Monthly retainers run from roughly $3,000 to $15,000, depending on cadence and how hands-on the person is. Senior people who bill by the hour typically charge $250 to $500.
